model-agency.lead: OpenUP model agency in Moscow. The site already ran on Tilda but looked dated and responded sluggishly. We redesigned the home page, header and footer, cleaned up the model catalogues and made the site bilingual.

facts.v: Refresh the site and open it to an English-speaking audience
Redesign and hand-written markup on top of Tilda
Home page, header, footer, catalogues, ru/en translation

blocks.title: The starting point
paragraphs: The agency's site ran on Tilda but looked dated: the styling lagged behind how model agencies present themselves today, and some of the content had not been updated in a long time.
The interface was slow to respond, and the navigation followed old patterns and no longer fit every section — and the agency has many: women, men, arrivals, new faces, international, production.

blocks.title: What we built
paragraphs: We designed a new home page, header and footer, then built them ourselves — not assembled from ready-made blocks, but written as markup and styles by hand on top of the builder.

The header gained a multi-level menu with dropdown sections, the mobile version a burger panel with social links, and on small screens the footer collapses its sections into an accordion. None of this comes with Tilda out of the box.

blocks.title: Model catalogues
paragraphs: The catalogues run on Tilda Store, and the default card layout did not suit the agency: a model roster is a showcase, not a product list.
We changed the display format, the card corner radii and their placement on the page, then went through the breakpoints separately so the grid holds on any screen.

blocks.title: Bilingual without a second site
paragraphs: Tilda offers no real bilingual support: the usual route is duplicating every page and then maintaining two copies of the site. Instead we wrote a script that translates the page on the fly when the ru or en button is clicked.

It carries its own dictionary of more than 800 pairs; strings missing from it are fetched from external translators with a fallback and then cached. Catalogue search is solved separately: model names are stored in Latin script, so a Russian query is rewritten inside the request to the server — visitors search in Russian and find what they need.

blocks.title: The outcome
paragraphs: Everything visible was refreshed: the home page, header, footer and catalogues. The navigation now fits every section of the agency, including the link to its children's branch.

The English version runs without a second site and without duplicate pages — there is one set of pages and one dictionary to maintain, and that dictionary is edited in a Google Sheet without touching code. The client does not share business metrics, so the numbers here are about our work only: everything described can be checked by opening the site.

skynia-hall.lead: SKYNIA HALL is an event venue next to Volgogradsky Prospekt metro: a main hall for 1,200 guests, a small hall and six meeting rooms. The old site showed the hall as one long page and didn't answer the key question — will it work for my wedding, conference or prom? facts.v: A site that sells the hall for a specific event and collects requests
Redesign and custom code blocks inside Tilda
Home page, 12 format pages, booking, legal pages

metrics.label: from choosing a hall to a request

blocks.title: The starting point
paragraphs: The venue had a draft of a new site and a clear feeling: it should look premium, not templated. The old Tilda page showed the hall, but guests had to call to find out whether their event would fit, what it cost and whether the date was free.
Booking lived on a separate page and requests had to be clarified by phone — a long way for someone who just wanted to ask about Saturday.

blocks.title: Design in three rounds
paragraphs: The first, light version felt too plain. The second — a serif and gold — was beautiful but hard to read. The third kept the dark background and gold accent but switched to Geologica and Golos Text: premium and easy to read on a phone.

We removed extra labels, left the first screen with a headline, one line and two buttons, and gave every section a clear next step. On desktop a short “Check available dates” form sits next to the hero.

blocks.title: Three-step booking
paragraphs: The separate booking page became a three-step window: hall and format, date and guests, contacts. A preliminary total is shown right away, the draft is saved if the guest gets distracted, and the selection can be sent to WhatsApp with one button.
On phones a smart bar sits at the bottom: its button label changes by section — “Book the hall”, “Pick a format”, “Ask a question” — and a round button opens call, WhatsApp and Telegram.

blocks.title: 12 pages for event formats
paragraphs: Wedding, corporate party, conference, prom, concert, training, exhibition and five more formats got their own pages: a headline for the search query, fitting photos, real events from the venue, answers to common questions and a form that already knows which event it's about.
Each page has its own meta tags, Schema.org markup and social cover, and they all share one frame: a new landing page is assembled from ready blocks rather than built from scratch.

blocks.title: Our own code inside Tilda
paragraphs: The venue wanted to stay on Tilda and edit texts and photos itself. So the design is built from custom blocks with our code: the editor works as usual and the layout holds on every screen.
The header, footer and booking window are shared across the site. Requests from every form land in Tilda CRM marked with the page and form they came from.

blocks.title: Speed, search and legal pages
paragraphs: Photos are served as WebP through Tilda's CDN, fonts are uploaded to the platform and unused code is stripped at build time: the mobile version scores 97 of 100 for performance in Lighthouse and 100 for accessibility, SEO and best practices.
We added a personal data policy, a separate consent document and a short cookie notice; Yandex Metrica starts only after it.

blocks.title: The outcome
paragraphs: The site now leads a guest from the event format to a request instead of just showing the hall. The venue updates texts, photos and prices itself, and new pages are built from the same block system.
The new version is being prepared to move to the main domain — we'll add a link to the live site after launch.

privacy.title: Personal Data Processing Policy
privacy.intro: This page describes what personal data the sandwor.online and sandwor.ru websites collect, why, to whom and where it is transferred, how long it is kept and how you can manage it. Consents to data processing — when sending a request and for cookies and web analytics — are separate documents. This is a translation; the Russian version prevails.

sections.heading: 1. Who processes the data
paragraphs: The personal data operator is {operator}, a self-employed professional income tax payer{inn_part} (the Operator). The Operator provides services under the sandwor name and owns the sandwor.online and sandwor.ru websites (the Site).

This policy is prepared under Russian Federal Law No. 152-FZ “On Personal Data” of 27.07.2006 and covers all data the Operator receives through the Site, the online chat on the Site and related contact channels.
Send questions about data processing, requests and consent withdrawals to {email}.

sections.heading: 2. Requests via the brief and materials
paragraphs: Data: name; phone number or Telegram username; preferred contact method; company name and number of people in sales (optional); selected services, task description and budget (optional). The request also stores the page it was sent from, the source of the visit (campaign tags, the first page on the Site and the domain you came from), the date and time of sending and a consent mark with its edition number.
Purpose: to review the request, contact you, prepare an offer and, if both parties agree, conclude and perform a services contract.

Legal basis: your consent (Art. 6(1)(1) of 152-FZ), given with a separate checkbox before sending the brief; once a contract is concluded — performance of a contract to which you are a party (Art. 6(1)(5)).

Processing: the request is sent over a secure connection (HTTPS) to the Site's server, checked for spam and stored in the amoCRM system, where only the Operator can see it. Requests from the Site are not forwarded to messengers or email.
Retention: if no contract is concluded — 1 year from the last contact; if it is — for the term of the contract and 5 years after its performance. The data is then deleted.

Checklists and other materials. If you request a material on the Site, the Operator receives your name, email address, the material, the page where it was offered and the source of the visit. Purpose: to provide the material and, if needed, answer questions about it; no promotional mailings are sent using this data. Basis — your separate consent (art. 6 part 1 item 1 of 152-FZ), given with a checkbox in the form. The data is stored in amoCRM for 1 year from the request.

sections.heading: 3. Online chat, email, phone and messengers
paragraphs: The Site has a contact button and an online chat by amoCRM. If you write in the chat, the Operator receives your name or nickname, the contact details you provide, message texts and attachments. The conversation is stored in amoCRM.

If you write to sandwor@mail.ru or call the number shown on the Site, the Operator receives your email address or phone number, your name and whatever you tell. Emails are stored in the Mail.ru email service (VK LLC), whose servers are located in Russia.

The Site also links to Telegram and WhatsApp. If you write to the Operator in a messenger, your data (name or nickname, phone number, messages and files) is processed in that messenger under its rules, and Telegram and WhatsApp servers are located outside Russia. This is a cross-border transfer of personal data on your initiative: if you don't want it, use the brief or the chat on the Site — they run on servers in Russia.
Purpose and basis: to answer your inquiry and correspond about it — on the basis of your consent expressed by sending a message.
Retention: 1 year from the last message unless a contract is concluded (then as in section 2).

sections.heading: 4. Cookies and web analytics
paragraphs: The Site uses Yandex Metrica (Yandex LLC): it collects cookies and browser identifiers, IP address, device, browser and operating system details, addresses of viewed pages and the referral source (including ad campaign tags), on-page actions — scrolling, clicks, navigation — and session recordings (Webvisor) without the contents of input fields.
Purpose: to understand how visitors use the Site, evaluate traffic sources and improve the Site.

Legal basis — your consent to cookies and web analytics. On your first visit the Site shows the notice “By continuing to use the site, you agree to the use of cookies and Yandex Metrica”. Metrica loads only when you continue to use the Site: after 5 seconds on a page or earlier — when you scroll, tap, press a key or go to another page. Following the "Learn more" link to these terms and reading them does not count as continued use. If you leave the Site earlier without doing anything, no data is sent to Metrica. The mark that the notice was shown is kept in the browser for 12 months; while it exists, Metrica loads right away on later visits.

How to opt out: disable cookies for the Site in your browser settings or clear the Site's data, install a tracker blocker or Yandex's official Metrica opt-out add-on. You can also withdraw consent by writing to {email}.
Retention: Metrica data is kept by Yandex under the service rules; the Operator uses it in aggregated form for no longer than 1 year. Yandex keeps Webvisor recordings for up to 15 days.

Technical data in the browser: the mark that the cookie notice was shown (localStorage, 12 months) and data the amoCRM chat button stores for the chat to work. They are needed for the Site to work and are not used for analytics.

sections.heading: 5. Server logs
paragraphs: With every request to the Site the server automatically records the IP address, date and time, page address and browser details. These logs are needed for the Site to work, to find failures and to defend against attacks. Legal basis — the Operator's legitimate interest in the secure operation of the Site (Art. 6(1)(7) of 152-FZ). Logs are kept for no more than 3 months and are not used to identify you.

sections.heading: 6. Who receives the data
paragraphs: The Operator does not sell personal data or share it for advertising. Data is processed on the Operator's behalf or with its involvement only by these services — to the extent needed for them to work:
amoCRM JSC (TIN 7709477879, Moscow) — the amoCRM system and the online chat on the Site: storing requests and conversations. Data is stored on servers in Russia.
Yandex LLC (TIN 7736207543, Moscow) — Yandex Metrica: processes data on the Operator's behalf under the service terms. Servers in Russia.
VK LLC (TIN 7743001840, Moscow) — the Mail.ru email service: storing the emails you send to the Operator. Servers in Russia.
Selectel JSC (TIN 7810962785) — hosting: the server the Site runs on and requests pass through. The server is located in Russia.

Telegram and WhatsApp — only if you write to the Operator in a messenger yourself (section 3). WhatsApp is owned by Meta Platforms, Inc., whose activities are recognised as extremist and banned in Russia.
Data may be disclosed to public authorities only where required by law.

sections.heading: 7. Where the data is stored
paragraphs: Recording, systematisation, accumulation, storage, clarification and retrieval of personal data of Russian citizens received through the brief, the chat and email take place in databases located in Russia: on the Site's server, in amoCRM and in the Mail.ru email service. A cross-border transfer is possible only when you correspond in messengers on your own initiative (section 3); the Operator notifies Roskomnadzor of it as required.

sections.heading: 8. What is done with the data
paragraphs: Collection, recording, systematisation, accumulation, storage, clarification (updating, changing), retrieval, use, transfer (provision, access) to the services in section 6, blocking, deletion and destruction. Processing is mixed: with and without automation, with transfer over the internet. Decisions with legal consequences for you are not made solely on the basis of automated processing.

sections.heading: 9. How the data is protected
paragraphs: Data is transferred only over a secure connection (HTTPS). Only the Operator has access to requests and conversations; CRM, hosting and analytics accounts are protected with passwords and two-factor authentication, and server access is key-based. The form filters spam and no unnecessary data is collected. The Operator keeps software up to date and, in case of a leak, notifies Roskomnadzor of the incident within 24 hours and of the investigation results within 72 hours.

sections.heading: 10. Your rights
paragraphs: You have the right to: find out whether and how your data is processed; get a copy of it; demand that data be clarified, blocked or deleted if it is incomplete, outdated, inaccurate or unlawfully obtained; withdraw consent; appeal the Operator's actions to Roskomnadzor or a court.

How: write to {email}, stating how to contact you and which data you mean (for example, the phone number from a request). The Operator replies within 10 business days; this may be extended by 5 business days with an explanation.

sections.heading: 11. Withdrawing consent and deletion
paragraphs: Consent is withdrawn by writing to {email}. The Operator stops processing and deletes the data within 30 days unless there are other lawful grounds to keep it (for example, a contract still being performed). Deletion is confirmed by a statement. Withdrawing consent to web analytics — see section 4.

sections.heading: 12. Changes to the policy
paragraphs: The Operator may update this policy, for example when connecting new services. A new edition applies from its publication on this page; the edition date is shown at the top. If the purposes or the data requiring consent change, the Operator will ask for consent again.

consent.title: Consent to Personal Data Processing
consent.intro: This page contains three separate consents: for processing data when you send a request, for cookies and web analytics, and when you request materials. Details are in the personal data policy.

sections.heading: 1. Consent when sending a request
paragraphs: By ticking “I consent to the processing of personal data” and sending the brief on sandwor.online or sandwor.ru, I freely, of my own will and in my own interest consent to {operator}, a self-employed professional income tax payer{inn_part} (the Operator), processing my personal data on the following terms.
Purpose: to review my request, contact me, prepare an offer and, if we agree, conclude and perform a services contract.

Data: name; phone number or Telegram username; preferred contact method; company name and number of people in sales, selected services, task description and budget — if I provided them; the page address, date and time of sending the request, the source of the visit (campaign tags, the first page and the domain I came from).

Actions: collection, recording, systematisation, accumulation, storage, clarification, retrieval, use, transfer (provision, access) to processors, blocking, deletion, destruction — with and without automation.
Processors engaged by the Operator: amoCRM JSC (TIN 7709477879) — the amoCRM system where the request is stored; Selectel JSC (TIN 7810962785) — website hosting. Data is stored on servers in Russia.

Term: the consent is valid for 1 year from sending the request, and if a contract is concluded — for its term and 5 years after its performance. I may withdraw consent at any time by writing to {email}; the Operator will then stop processing and delete the data within 30 days unless there are other lawful grounds to keep it.

sections.heading: 2. Consent to cookies and web analytics
paragraphs: By continuing to use the site after the cookie notice (after 5 seconds on a page, when scrolling, tapping, pressing a key, clicking “OK” or going to another page), I consent to {operator} (the Operator) processing the data collected by Yandex Metrica.
Purpose: analysing traffic and how visitors use the site, evaluating traffic sources and improving the site.

Data: cookies and browser identifiers, IP address, device, browser and operating system details, addresses of viewed pages, the referral source and ad campaign tags, on-page actions and session recordings (Webvisor) without the contents of input fields.
Actions: collection, recording, storage, use in aggregated form, transfer to the processor — with automation.
Processor: Yandex LLC (TIN 7736207543) processes data on the Operator's behalf under the Yandex Metrica terms of use. Servers in Russia.

Term: 1 year; the mark that the notice was shown is kept in the browser for 12 months. You can withdraw consent by disabling cookies for the site in your browser or clearing the site's data, installing Yandex's official Metrica opt-out add-on, or writing to {email}.

sections.heading: 3. Consent when requesting materials
paragraphs: By ticking "I consent to the processing of my personal data" in the form for receiving a material (for example, a checklist) on sandwor.online or sandwor.ru, I freely, of my own will and in my own interest give consent to {operator_dat} (the Operator) to process my personal data on the following terms.
Purpose: to provide me with the requested material and, if needed, to answer my questions about it. No promotional mailings are sent using this data.
Data: name; email address; which material I requested and on which page; the source of the visit (campaign tags, the first page and the domain I came from); the date and time of the request.

Actions: collection, recording, systematisation, accumulation, storage, clarification, retrieval, use, transfer (provision, access) to processors, blocking, deletion, destruction — with and without automation.
Processors: amoCRM JSC (TIN 7709477879) — the amoCRM system where the request is stored; Selectel JSC (TIN 7810962785) — website hosting. Data is stored on servers in Russia.
Term: 1 year from the date of the request. I can withdraw consent at any time by writing to {email}; the Operator will then stop processing and delete the data within 30 days.
